scope: Proposition 7.4 of the manuscript “The Singer conjecture in dimension four” (preprints/The-Singer-conjecture-in-dimension-four-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 315 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 179f73885d0c7f47), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are a subgroup H ≤ Γ, a compact space Y = H ⊔L ⊂ X, and a connected H-graph K with vertex set I ⊂ Y , with the following properties. 1. Y = H X . The points of H are isolated in Y , and L is a nondegenerate continuum without cut points satisfying dim L ≤ 1, Ȟ1 (L; F2) = 0. 2. If hn → a ∈ L and h−1 n → b ∈ L, then hn converges to the constant map a, uniformly on compact subsets of Y \ {b}. 3. The graph K has finitely many H-orbits of vertices and edges. Either I = H, or I ⊂ L. Every point of L is the limit of a sequence of distinct vertices in I. 4. For each fixed w ∈ I, ρ(hw, h) −→ 0 as h −→ ∞ in H. (7.2) 5. For every x ∈ L and every neighborhood W of x in Y , there is a neighborhood V of x in Y such that any two vertices of I ∩ V can be joined by a path in K all of whose vertices belong to W. 6. If I ⊂ L, then for each p ∈ I there is an infinite-order element h ∈ Hp such that hj z −→ p (j −→ +∞), z ∈ L. No finite generation assumption on H or local finiteness assumption on K is included in these conclusions.
